recipes.title: Mercimek Çorbası (Red Lentil Soup)
recipes.dish_alt: A white bowl of golden Mercimek Çorbası (Turkish red lentil soup) with a lemon wedge on the side
recipes.prep_label: Prep — The Pul Biber & Mint Tarka
recipes.prep_alt: A bowl of Turkish lentil soup with a swirl of sizzled butter, pul biber, and dried mint drizzled on top

sections.heading: Steps
items: Warm the olive oil in a pot over medium heat. Add the onion and carrot and cook 4-5 minutes until softened.
Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato paste, cumin, and paprika, cooking 1 minute until deep red and fragrant.
Add the red lentils, potato, and stock. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer 20-25 minutes until completely soft.
Blend the soup until smooth and velvety, using an immersion blender or a standard blender in batches.
Return to low heat, thin with a splash of water or stock if needed, and season with salt.
Make the tarka: melt the butter in a small pan, add the dried mint and pul biber, and sizzle 20-30 seconds until fragrant.
Ladle into bowls, drizzle the mint-pul biber butter on top, and serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.title: Turkish Köfte with Rice Pilaf
recipes.dish_alt: Grilled Turkish köfte meatballs served with rice pilaf, grilled green peppers, tomato, and onion
recipes.prep_alt: Raw seasoned köfte meat shaped onto skewers, ready for the grill

sections.heading: Steps
items: In a bowl, combine the ground beef, grated onion, garlic, breadcrumbs, cumin, paprika, oregano, parsley, salt, and pepper. Mix and knead briefly until well combined.
Shape into oval or flattened round patties about the size of your palm. Rest 10 minutes in the fridge if time allows.
Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Sear the köfte 3-4 minutes per side until deeply browned and cooked through with no pink in the center.
Meanwhile, make the pilaf: melt the butter with the olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the orzo and toast 1-2 minutes until golden brown.
Add the rice and stir to coat every grain in the fat, toasting 1-2 minutes more.
Pour in the hot chicken stock and salt, bring to a boil, then cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer 15 minutes without lifting the lid.
Remove from heat, keep covered, and let rest 5-10 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Serve the köfte hot alongside the rice pilaf.

recipes.title: Karnıyarık (Stuffed Eggplant with Ground Beef)
recipes.dish_alt: Karnıyarık — a split, stuffed eggplant filled with spiced ground beef, tomato, and pepper, in tomato sauce
recipes.prep_alt: A close-up of the split eggplant stuffed with ground beef filling and topped with tomato and green pepper

sections.heading: Steps
items: Peel the eggplants in alternating strips, then slit each lengthwise down the middle without cutting all the way through.
Salt the eggplants and let sit 15 minutes to draw out bitterness, then rinse and pat dry.
Shallow-fry the eggplants in olive oil over medium heat, turning, until softened and lightly golden all over, 8-10 minutes. Arrange in a baking dish, gently pressing open the slit.
Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F).
In the same pan, cook the onion 3-4 minutes until soft, then add the garlic and green pepper, cooking 2 minutes more.
Add the ground beef and cook, breaking it up, until browned with no pink remaining.
Stir in the tomato paste and red pepper paste, cooking 1 minute until deep red and fragrant.
Add the diced tomatoes, cumin, parsley, salt, and pepper, and simmer 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
Spoon the meat filling generously into the slit of each eggplant, mounding it on top.
Top each stuffed eggplant with a tomato slice and a strip of green pepper. Pour the water or stock into the bottom of the baking dish.
Bake 20-25 minutes until the eggplant is fully tender and the filling is bubbling.
Serve hot, with rice pilaf and yogurt on the side if you like.

recipes.title: Tavuk Şiş (Chicken Shish Kebab)
recipes.dish_alt: Grilled Tavuk Şiş chicken kebab pieces served with flatbread, tomato, salad, and a spiced tomato relish
recipes.prep_alt: Grilled chicken shish kebab pieces served with rice pilaf, yogurt, and tomato

sections.heading: Steps
items: In a bowl, whisk together the yogurt, olive oil, tomato paste, garlic, paprika, cumin, pul biber, oregano, salt, and pepper.
Add the cubed chicken and toss until every piece is coated. Cover and marinate in the fridge at least 1 hour.
Thread the marinated chicken onto skewers, alternating with pieces of bell pepper and cherry tomatoes.
Heat a grill, grill pan, or broiler to high heat.
Grill the skewers 10-12 minutes total, turning every few minutes, until deeply charred in spots and cooked through with no pink at the center.
While the chicken grills, toss the sliced red onion with sumac and a pinch of salt for a quick onion salad.
Serve the skewers hot with the sumac onion salad and lemon wedges for squeezing over.

recipes.title: Turkish Chicken Güveç (Chicken & Vegetable Stew)
recipes.dish_alt: A bowl of Turkish güveç-style meat and vegetable stew — tender meat, potatoes, and carrots in a rich tomato sauce
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Meat & Vegetables in the Güveç Pot
recipes.prep_alt: Chunks of meat, potatoes, and vegetables simmering together in a traditional güveç dish

sections.heading: Steps
items: Warm the olive oil in a wide pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the chicken and sear 3-4 minutes until lightly golden.
Add the onion and garlic, cooking 3-4 minutes until softened.
Stir in the tomato paste and red pepper paste, cooking 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the bell peppers, potato, tomatoes, bay leaf, oregano, dried mint, salt, and pepper.
Pour in the water or stock, stir well, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and simmer on low heat 35-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is fully cooked and potatoes are tender.
Uncover and simmer 5-10 more minutes to thicken the sauce slightly.
Discard the bay leaf, taste and adjust seasoning, then serve hot with crusty bread.

recipes.title: Lahmacun (Turkish Flatbread with Spiced Meat)
recipes.dish_alt: A single Lahmacun Turkish flatbread topped with spiced minced meat, served with fresh salad
recipes.prep_alt: Multiple rounds of thin lahmacun dough topped with spiced meat, ready to bake

sections.heading: Steps
items: Make the dough: dissolve the yeast in the warm water and let sit 5 minutes until foamy.
Combine the flour and salt in a bowl, add the yeast water and olive oil, and knead 5-6 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise in a warm spot 20-25 minutes until slightly puffy.
Meanwhile, finely chop the onion, tomato, garlic, and parsley together until they form a wet, finely minced paste.
Combine this vegetable mixture with the ground lamb, tomato paste, red pepper paste, paprika, pul biber, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Preheat the oven as hot as it goes (240-260°C / 465-500°F) with a baking sheet or pizza stone inside.
Divide the dough into portions and roll each one out very thin, almost paper-thin, on a floured surface.
Spread a thin, even layer of the meat topping all the way to the edges of each dough round.
Transfer the topped rounds onto the hot baking sheet and bake 7-9 minutes until the edges are crisp and the meat is fully cooked.
Serve immediately, rolled up with a squeeze of lemon, fresh parsley, and sliced onion inside.

recipes.title: Turkish Pide (Cheese & Beef Flatbread)
recipes.dish_alt: A whole kıymalı (ground beef) Turkish pide, boat-shaped and sliced, served with salad and pickled peppers
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Kıymalı Pide Fresh from the Oven
recipes.prep_alt: A boat-shaped ground beef pide fresh from the oven, topped with green peppers

sections.heading: Steps
items: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the warm water; let sit 5 minutes until foamy.
Mix in the yogurt, olive oil, flour, and salt, and knead 6-8 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise in a warm place 45-60 minutes until roughly doubled.
Meanwhile, mix the ground beef, onion, green pepper, tomato, tomato paste, red pepper paste, paprika, pul biber, salt, and pepper to make the filling.
Preheat the oven to 230°C (450°F) with a baking sheet inside.
Punch down the dough and roll each portion into a long oval, about 1cm thick.
Spread the meat filling down the center, leaving a 2-3cm border, and sprinkle the shredded kaşar cheese over the filling.
Fold the two long edges of the dough up and over the filling, pinching the ends together to form a boat shape.
Brush the exposed crust with beaten egg for shine.
Bake 12-15 minutes until the crust is deep golden and the filling is bubbling and cooked through.
Brush the hot crust with melted butter as soon as it comes out of the oven, then slice and serve.

recipes.title: Sütlaç (Turkish Rice Pudding) (Bonus)
recipes.dish_alt: Sütlaç, Turkish rice pudding, served in a glass dish dusted with cinnamon
recipes.prep_alt: Ramekins of rice pudding with caramelized, browned tops fresh from the broiler before chilling

sections.heading: Steps
items: Rinse the rice and simmer it in the water over low heat, covered, 10-12 minutes until just tender.
Add the milk and bring to a gentle simmer, stirring occasionally so the rice doesn't stick.
Whisk the cornstarch with a splash of cold milk until smooth, then stir this slurry into the pot.
Add the sugar and simmer 10-15 minutes, stirring frequently, until thickened to a pourable custard consistency.
Temper the egg yolk with a spoonful of the hot mixture, then stir it back into the pot (optional — the pudding sets from the cornstarch alone).
Stir in the vanilla extract and simmer 2 more minutes.
Pour the pudding into individual ramekins or bowls.
For the traditional caramelized top, place under a hot broiler 2-3 minutes until brown spots form — or skip and simply dust with cinnamon.
Let cool to room temperature, then refrigerate at least 2 hours until fully chilled and set.
Sprinkle with ground cinnamon just before serving.
